topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: In hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring, the choice of Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) versus Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites significantly impacts latency and coverage. LEO satellites offer lower latency due to their shorter distance from Earth, reducing propagation delay and enabling real-time data transmission. However, this comes at the cost of more frequent re-pointing and increased system complexity. In contrast, GEO satellites provide large stationary footprints but suffer from high latency due to their greater distance from Earth. This results in increased signal delays, which can impact the real-time monitoring and control of substations. The choice between GEO and LEO orbits depends on the specific requirements of the rural substation monitoring system, with LEO being more suitable for applications requiring low latency.
